# Overview

`qtlRegressionStats()` fits, for each requested SNP-gene pair, a linear
model of phenotype on genotype plus all covariates stored in the
`tQTLExperiment`'s `colData`:

```
phenotype ~ genotype + <covariates>
```

It exists alongside `tensorQTL`, not as a replacement for it: `tensorQTL` is
the tool for mapping cis-QTLs genome-wide, while `qtlRegressionStats()` gives
full `lm()` output (coefficients, standard errors, t-statistics for every
covariate, not just genotype) for a targeted set of pairs, in-process in R.
This is useful for follow-up on specific genes, for building the input to
[`qtlPCABrowser()`](pcaBrowser.html), and any time you want the whole
regression table rather than tensorQTL's genotype-only summary.

Pairs can be processed in parallel across phenotypes (or, in gene mode,
across variants) via `BiocParallel::bplapply()`.

```{r loaddata, message=FALSE}
library(tQTLExperiment)
library(GenomicRanges)
library(S4Vectors)
```

# Example data

The small chr22 example dataset (20 genes, 100 samples) ships with the
package and needs no external downloads.

```{r construct}
exdir <- system.file("extdata", package = "tQTLExperiment")
tqe <- tQTLExperiment(
    plinkPrefix = file.path(exdir, "chr22-n100"),
    phenoFile   = file.path(exdir, "mean-pheno-n100.bed"),
    covFile     = file.path(exdir, "cov-n100-tqtl.tsv"),
    genome      = "hg38"
)
tqe
colnames(colData(tqe))
```

The covariates here are a mix of a fixed effect (`sex`), a continuous
covariate (`age`), and expression/genotype PCs -- no factor-expanded
columns, so `qtlRegressionStats()`'s output has one column per covariate
rather than one per factor level.

# Two ways to specify pairs

## Explicit pairs

Supply a data frame with `phenotype_id` and `variant_id` columns naming
exactly the pairs to fit.

```{r pairs}
pairs <- data.frame(
    phenotype_id = rownames(tqe)[1],
    variant_id   = mcols(tqtlVariantRanges(tqe))[["snp_id"]][1]
)
qtlRegressionStats(tqe, pairs)
```

## Gene symbol and cis window

Alternatively, supply `symbol` and a `window` (bp) to fit every variant
within that window of the gene's start. This requires a `gene_name` column
in `rowRanges(tqe)`, added by `addGeneSymbols()`.

```{r symcheck}
if (requireNamespace("EnsDb.Hsapiens.v79", quietly = TRUE)) {
    tqe <- addGeneSymbols(tqe)
    head(mcols(rowRanges(tqe))[, c("phenotype_id", "gene_name")])
}
```

```{r genemode, eval=requireNamespace("EnsDb.Hsapiens.v79", quietly = TRUE)}
res_gene <- qtlRegressionStats(tqe, symbol = "TPTEP1", window = 1000000L)
dim(res_gene)
head(res_gene)
```

`pairs` and `symbol` are mutually exclusive -- supply exactly one.

# Output shape: t_only and wideFormat

Two arguments control the shape of the result:

- `t_only`: `TRUE` (default) returns just the t-statistic
  (`estimate / std.error`) per term; `FALSE` also returns the estimate,
  standard error, raw t-statistic, and p-value.
- `wideFormat`: `TRUE` (default) pivots to one row per pair, with one
  (or two, if `t_only = FALSE`) columns per model term; `FALSE` returns
  the long tidy form, one row per pair x term.

```{r shapes, eval=requireNamespace("EnsDb.Hsapiens.v79", quietly = TRUE)}
# long form, full statistics -- one row per pair x covariate
long <- qtlRegressionStats(tqe, symbol = "TPTEP1", t_only = FALSE, wideFormat = FALSE)
head(long)

# wide form, t-statistics only (the input qtlPCABrowser() expects)
head(qtlRegressionStats(tqe, symbol = "TPTEP1"))
```

The wide, `t_only = TRUE` form is exactly what
[`qtlPCABrowser()`](pcaBrowser.html) and `collapseFactorTstats()` expect as
input: one row per SNP-gene pair, one `<term>.t` column per covariate.

# Collapsing factor-expanded columns

When a covariate matrix includes a multi-level factor (e.g. `batch` or
`population`), `model.matrix()` expands it into several dummy columns, so
the wide `qtlRegressionStats()` output carries one `t.<var><level>` column
per level. `collapseFactorTstats()` replaces each such group with a single
root-mean-square summary column, which keeps a PCA on t-statistics from
being dominated by however many levels a factor happens to have.

```{r collapse, eval=requireNamespace("EnsDb.Hsapiens.v79", quietly = TRUE)}
wide <- qtlRegressionStats(tqe, symbol = "TPTEP1")
names(wide)
# no factor-expanded columns in this toy covariate set, so this is a no-op
head(collapseFactorTstats(wide))
```

On the MAGE chr17 dataset used in the main vignette, the covariate matrix
includes `factor_batch_*` and `population*` dummy columns, and
`collapseFactorTstats()` reduces each group to `t.batch` and
`t.population`. See `?collapseFactorTstats` for the pattern arguments.

# Parallelization

`BPPARAM` is passed straight to `BiocParallel::bplapply()`. Pairs are
grouped by phenotype: with multiple phenotypes, groups are distributed
across workers; in gene-symbol mode (a single phenotype, many variants),
the inner loop over variants is parallelized instead.

```{r parallel, eval=FALSE}
qtlRegressionStats(
    tqe,
    symbol  = "TPTEP1",
    BPPARAM = BiocParallel::MulticoreParam(4)
)
```

# Chromosome-naming caveat

`rowRanges(tqe)` built from a `SummarizedExperiment` typically carries
UCSC-style seqnames (`"chr17"`), while `tqtlVariantRanges(tqe)` reflects the
PLINK `.bim` convention of bare chromosome numbers (`"17"`).
`qtlRegressionStats()` normalizes both by stripping any leading `"chr"`
before comparing when `symbol` is used to select the cis window. If you
write code that intersects `rowRanges(tqe)` and `tqtlVariantRanges(tqe)`
directly, apply the same normalization:

```{r seqfix, eval=FALSE}
sub("^chr", "", as.character(seqnames(gr)))
```
